name: Clean-English formalization: the live SymbolicLM rules on valid, clean English only, versus the full English suites
registered_by: clean-english-agent (owner decision of 2026-09-30, journaled: formalization evaluation focuses on valid, clean English)

owner_requests.decision_2026_09_30: Formalization focuses only on VALID, CLEAN ENGLISH. Romanian, mixed Romanian/English (romgleza) and badly written English (typos, garbled, confusing input) leave the formalization evaluation; they will be handled by a separate textToCleanEnglish service in the chat UI under user control (a different agent's task, text-to-clean-english-v1). The fine-tuned Gemma3-270M proofreader stays only as a simplifier of valid English for SymbolicLM. Goal: focus on justified problems -- formalizing valid English text.

kind: evaluation-only (CPU inference; no training, no GPU, no LLM judge)
frozen_before_results: This preregistration is written in the same working session as the first exploratory runs (the four-partition classifier and the corpus build happened first, since the metric cannot be defined without it); it is not frozen before any row was seen, unlike eval-symbolic-lm-v1's roA/roB split. The freeze that matters here is code identity, not blindness to the data: `tools/research/clean-english-eval.mjs` `codeHashes()` (reused from tools/research/symbolic-lm-eval.mjs) records the SHA-256 of every file that decides a SymbolicLM output in every run manifest, and the live lib/ud-to-sop + training/python/ud_parse_worker.py were independently verified byte-identical to the frozen eval/reports/current/baseline-ud-rules/frozen-rules-v1.4/SHA256SUMS snapshot before any run (recorded in topic notes, topic clean-english). This is recorded as a deviation from the ideal frozen-before-results template, not concealed.

system_under_test.symbolic_lm: lib/symbolic-lm/ direct route (route: 'direct', language: 'auto'), CPU; live lib/ud-to-sop verified identical to frozen-rules-v1.4
system_under_test.clean_english_filter: tools/datasets/clean-english.mjs classifyPartition: gate (a) no generator noise/typo/code-switch tag, (b) lib/languages-util spellfix.fix() proposes no correction, (c) every non-name non-numeric non-quoted word token is labelled `en` by LanguagesUtil identify(), (d) eval/reference-free.mjs gibberishVerdict() is not `gibberish`; grammar check (e) not implemented locally (dependencies.md follow-up)
system_under_test.corpus: datasets/clean-english/{train,dev}.jsonl and the sealed eval/suites/clean-english/test.jsonl (clean_en rows of formalizer-v1 train/dev and of the three sealed suites formalizer-v1, formalizer-ood-v1, formalizer-wild-v1), built by tools/datasets/build-clean-english.mjs
system_under_test.input: the row's message (question) only (DS014 model boundary)

sets.clean: eval/suites/clean-english/test.jsonl (clean_en rows of the three sealed suites; 2,484 rows at build time)
sets.full-en: clean_en + noisy_en rows of the same three sealed suites (row.language en, not mixed by the classifier; 3,610 rows), for the 'how much of the earlier failure was input noise' comparison
sets.stages: nested stratified prefixes by question_type (tools/research/ud-baseline-eval.mjs stages, seed 20260930): 100, 300, full

hypotheses.H1: Strict execution-equivalence on `clean` is higher than on `full-en`: the paired-style gap (independent-samples delta, since the two sets overlap but are not a paired design) is positive and its 95% interval does not include 0, showing that at least part of the earlier full-suite failure was input noise, not a parser/rules defect on valid English.
hypotheses.H2: The frame-normalized score (sop/frames.mjs normalizeProgram) on `clean` is higher than the strict score on `clean` by a margin outside the paired bootstrap 95% interval's lower bound of 0, showing host-side synonym/frame normalization recovers some of the remaining gap.
hypotheses.H3: The top failure patterns on `clean` (structural blame via tools/research/symbolic-layers-diff.mjs diffCategories/classesOf) are dominated by rules/parser classes (R/P), not by gold-convention or language classes (C/L), supporting 'these are justified problems to fix next'.

metrics.primary: execution_equivalent (strict) on `clean`, full stage, per suite and per question_type; formalizer-v1/formalizer-ood-v1 rows scored by eval/run.mjs evaluate() against their verification world, formalizer-wild-v1 rows (no verification world) scored by tools/eval/wild-suite.mjs scoreAgainstAccepted (accepted_match) against every accepted gold, pooled
secondary: the same metrics on `full-en`, for the noise-vs-defect comparison

proofreader effect (rewrite backend, gated and always-on) on the clean_en subset of the eval-proofreader-e2e-v1 stage-300 stratified sample of formalizer-v1 (reusing its already-computed baseline/always-on predictions, filtered post hoc by the clean-english classifier, since a full separate clean-english x proofreader run was not budgeted in this session)
top-10 structural blame patterns on clean misses (tools/research/symbolic-layers-diff.mjs, no LLM judge)
metrics.intervals: paired cluster bootstrap over semantic_case_id where the comparison is paired (frame vs strict on the same rows; tools/research/symbolic-lm-eval.mjs pairedDelta), Wilson 95% intervals for single proportions (tools/research/symbolic-lm-eval.mjs wilson)

stopping_rules.stages: clean and full-en are each scored at 100, 300 and (if not already decisive/futile) the full set
stopping_rules.broken: stop and report if more than 20% of the first 100 outputs of a set are invalid or empty (tools/research/clean-english-eval.mjs conditionCheck)
stopping_rules.decisive_or_futile: at stage 300, if the clean-vs-full-en gap's 95% interval already excludes 0 by a practically relevant margin (>=3 points) or the interval already spans a range that makes the full-set run uninformative for the primary decision (justified-problems triage), stop at 300 and record the reason instead of spending the ~2h CPU budget on the full ~6,000-row run
stopping_rules.record: every stop is recorded with its stage, numbers and reason in the journal, the topic notes (topic clean-english), this experiment record and eval/reports/current/clean-english/summary.md

out_of_scope: training or fine-tuning any model (owner prohibition, AGENTS.md rule 3)
Romanian, mixed and noisy-English formalization accuracy (handled by textToCleanEnglish / text-to-clean-english-v1, a separate service and a separate agent's task)
